## Capstone Requirement

---

All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier).

notes.text: The Bachelor of Arts in History requires students to take 10 courses (40 units).
notes.source_line: The Bachelor of Arts in History requires students to take 10 courses (40 units).

notes.text: The History major offers students a means to encounter the peoples and cultures of the past and develop critical thinking, research and writing skills essential for understanding the present. The program exposes students to underlying connections between the study of past times and places and the roots of that study in human concerns about values, identities, issues and policies.
notes.source_line: The History major offers students a means to encounter the peoples and cultures of the past and develop critical thinking, research and writing skills essential for understanding the present. The program exposes students to underlying connections between the study of past times and places and the roots of that study in human concerns about values, identities, issues and policies.

notes.text: In their lower-division courses, majors will have the opportunity to explore the histories of different cultures across time. Students at the upper-division level hone their knowledge of different cultures and societies, while also learning how to do history. When they begin to take seminar courses (400 level), they will apply that knowledge to a substantial works of independent research.

Students at the upper-division level hone their knowledge of different cultures and societies, while also learning how to do history. When they begin to take seminar courses (400 level), they will apply that knowledge to a substantial works of independent research.

notes.text: All majors are required to complete HIST 201 Approaches to History. It is recommended that students complete HIST 201 early in their course of study.
notes.source_line: All majors are required to complete HIST 201 Approaches to History. It is recommended that students complete HIST 201 early in their course of study.

notes.text: Students can take up to three additional lower-division survey courses. However, if they prefer to take upper-division courses instead, they may.

notes.text: The Department of History will accept scores of 4 or 5 on Advanced Placement European History, Advanced Placement United States History or Advanced Placement World History as a substitute for one course requirement at the lower-division level.

notes.text: Six upper-division courses are required, of which at least two must be 400-levels. No more than 4 units of HIST 490x Directed Research may be counted as satisfying the upper-division seminar requirement.

notes.text: For geographic breadth, majors must take at least one course from four geographic areas. Those areas and the classes that fulfill them are listed below. Majors must also take two class that focus on the period before 1800 and two that focus on the period after 1800 to show temporal breadth. The courses that cover those periods are listed below. A single course may fulfill both a geographic and temporal requirement.

notes.text: All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier). There are two ways to complete the history capstone: a History Honors Thesis or a History Capstone Exercise.
notes.source_line: All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier). There are two ways to complete the history capstone: a History Honors Thesis or a History Capstone Exercise.

notes.text: The History Honors Thesis is a substantial work of scholarship based on original primary source research and/or extensive analysis of a methodological or historiographical issue. To apply for the Honors program, students need a 3.5 or higher GPA in all USC history coursework (although this can be waived in certain cases). They also need to take HIST 492 , both in the fall and spring semester. Those who take this track will be considered for honors in the major. Taking HIST 492 will count as their Capstone.

They also need to take HIST 492 , both in the fall and spring semester. Those who take this track will be considered for honors in the major. Taking HIST 492 will count as their Capstone.

notes.text: The History Capstone Exercise is a way for students to reflect upon what they have learned as a history major. They will need to fill out a google form (or submit their answers in essay form) where they will reflect upon the classes they took, the papers wrote, and the skills they have developed. They will also attend one of the “Capstone Conversation” events scheduled throughout the year, where they will discuss their answers and their experiences as a major in a larger group setting. The questions and google document link will be posted on the website under Undergraduate Capstone.

notes.text: All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier). There are two ways to complete the history capstone: a History Honors Thesis or a History Capstone Exercise.
notes.source_line: All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier). There are two ways to complete the history capstone: a History Honors Thesis or a History Capstone Exercise.

notes.text: The History Honors Thesis is a substantial work of scholarship based on original primary source research and/or extensive analysis of a methodological or historiographical issue. To apply for the Honors program, students need a 3.5 or higher GPA in all USC history coursework (although this can be waived in certain cases). They also need to take HIST 492 , both in the fall and spring semester. Those who take this track will be considered for honors in the major. Taking HIST 492 will count as their Capstone.

notes.text: The History Capstone Exercise is a way for students to reflect upon what they have learned as a history major. They will need to fill out a google form (or submit their answers in essay form) where they will reflect upon the classes they took, the papers wrote, and the skills they have developed. They will also attend one of the “Capstone Conversation” events scheduled throughout the year, where they will discuss their answers and their experiences as a major in a larger group setting. The questions and google document link will be posted on the website under Undergraduate Capstone.
